Unstable ranking (tau=-0.014) and correlated errors (mean_corr=0.79) suggest diversity-seeking combination is appropriate; DBA explicitly trades off error vs. diversity unlike the rank-based trimmed_mean/median already tested.

Proportional inverse-error weighting tests whether smooth downweighting of high-error models (vs hard trimming) helps given unstable ranking and 0.59 relative spread; different mechanism from trimmed_mean/median.
Simplest robust baseline to calibrate how much trimming/median actually contributes over plain averaging, given unstable ranking and low predictability.
Restrict to top-7 by SMAPE (cluster-diverse: NaiveMA, FT_catboost, THETA, DWT_catboost, ARIMA, ETS, FT_rf) then trim worst ~1 each end to test if a narrower robust pool beats full-pool trimmed_mean
Per-horizon top-3 (smape) adapts to unstable cross-window ranking; tests whether horizon-specific model selection beats flat robust aggregation on this mixed-regime series.
Lighter trim keeps more model diversity given unstable rankings (tau~0); tests whether 0.2 was too aggressive

Softmax weighting on full pool: smoother emphasis on better models than inverse_error (already tested at 1.0068), testing whether relative emphasis on trend-capturing models (trend_strength=0.9996) helps while preserving robustness against unstable rankings (tau=-0.014)

Error-trend weights capture which models are improving vs degrading across windows; complementary to level-based weights already tested. Motivated by unstable rankings (tau=-0.014) and visible trend in window SMAPEs (NaiveMovingAverage improving, ONLY_FT_rf degrading).
Unstable rankings (tau=-0.014) and strong trend suggest different models win at different horizons; hard per-horizon assignment is a fundamentally different strategy from soft aggregation
Higher trim (0.3 vs 0.2) to counteract high error correlation (mean_corr=0.79) and low predictability; tests whether removing more redundant forecasts improves robustness

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.929. Series context: trend strength 0.9996 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.014); 4 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.59.
